query: 2025 European Junior Swimming Championships Samorin Slovakia: Russia AIN neutral athletes gold medal results day by day. Which events did Russia win gold (5 total) and on which days? Also note 2021 Rome Russia 11 golds. Was Russia's gold haul back-loaded toward later days of the meet?
answer:
Report delivered above. Three things worth flagging from the research:

1. **The 2025 answer is precise**: golds on days 2, 3, 5, 6, 6 — cumulative 0-1-2-2-3-5. All 13 AIN medals reconcile exactly against the official table.

2. **The "back-loaded" premise doesn't survive the 2021 comparison.** Russia's 11 golds in Rome were distributed 1-2-2-2-2-2 — as flat as a distribution can be. So back-loading isn't a stable Russian trait; what *is* stable is that their strongest event group (distance freestyle) sits late in the six-day program, and day 6 always carries the most finals (12 of 42).

3. **The 2026 meet has already been held** (Munich, 7–12 July 2026) and the Neutral Athletes won 15 golds / 36 medals, topping the table. If this research was feeding a forecast on that event, it's resolved. The 5 → 15 jump is largely explained by relay eligibility returning after the 5 Feb 2026 EA rule change — AIN had zero relay medals in 2025 and four relay golds in 2026.

key_facts: 2025 European Junior Swimming Championships: 1–6 July 2025, X-bionic Sphere, Šamorín, Slovakia; 51st edition; 42 medal events (34 individual + 8 relays); 666 swimmers from 51 countries.
AIN (Neutral Individual Athletes, i.e. Russian swimmers) finished 2nd on the 2025 medal table with 5 gold, 4 silver, 4 bronze = 13 medals, behind Great Britain (9-5-5, 19 medals).

The five 2025 AIN golds and their days: Day 2 (Wed 2 Jul) Boys 50m backstroke — Georgii Iakovlev, 25.04; Day 3 (Thu 3 Jul) Boys 200m IM — Mikhail Shcherbakov, 1:59.04 Championship Record; Day 5 (Sat 5 Jul) Girls 800m freestyle — Sofia Diakova, 8:27.78; Day 6 (Sun 6 Jul) Girls 400m freestyle — Sofia Diakova, 4:07.06; Day 6 (Sun 6 Jul) Boys 400m freestyle — Grigorii Vekovishchev, 3:48.71.
2025 AIN cumulative gold count by day: 0 – 1 – 2 – 2 – 3 – 5. AIN won zero medals of any colour on Day 1 (3 finals) and Day 4 (8 finals).

Full 2025 AIN medal ledger by day: Day 1 = 0-0-0; Day 2 = 1G/0S/2B (Iakovlev gold + Shcherbakov bronze 50 back, Diakova bronze 200 free); Day 3 = 1G/1S/0B (Shcherbakov gold 200 IM, Manokhina tied silver 50 free); Day 4 = 0-0-0; Day 5 = 1G/1S/1B (Diakova gold 800 free, Vekovishchev silver 800 free, Fokina bronze 200 fly); Day 6 = 2G/2S/1B.
In the 2025 girls 50m freestyle, Kira Manokhina (AIN) and Theodora Taylor (GBR) tied for silver at 25.12 behind Martine Damborg (DEN) 25.00; no bronze was awarded.
2025 back-loading verdict: mild. 3 of 5 golds (60%) came on days 5–6 and 2 of 5 (40%) on the final day, but 17 of 42 finals (40%) and 12 of 42 (29%) were scheduled in those windows respectively.

AIN won ZERO relay medals in 2025 — all 13 medals were individual — so their addressable pool was 34 individual finals, of which 14 (41%) fell on days 5–6. Per-event gold rate: 2/20 (10%) on days 1–4 vs 3/14 (21%) on days 5–6.

The apparent back-loading in 2025 is driven by event mix rather than momentum: AIN strength was concentrated in distance freestyle (Diakova, Vekovishchev, Misharina), and the 800m frees were scheduled day 5 with the 400m frees on day 6.
2021 Rome (6–11 July 2021, Stadio Olimpico del Nuoto): Russia won 11 gold, 9 silver, 6 bronze = 26 medals, topping the medal table and winning the Team Trophy. 42 events, 127 medals total.

Russia's 11 golds in 2021 were distributed almost perfectly uniformly by day: 1, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2 (cumulative 1-3-5-7-9-11). 2021 was NOT back-loaded — only 36% of golds came in the last two days, below the share of finals held then.

2021 Russia golds by day: Day 1 (6 Jul) Men's 4×100 free relay; Day 2 (7 Jul) Women's 100 free (Klepikova 54.75) + Mixed 4×100 free relay; Day 3 (8 Jul) Women's 200 fly (Markova 2:08.41 CR) + Mixed 4×100 medley relay (3:50.25); Day 4 (9 Jul) Men's 50 back (Tkachev 25.14) + Men's 4×200 free relay (7:21.06); Day 5 (10 Jul) Women's 50 fly (Klepikova) + Women's 4×100 free relay; Day 6 (11 Jul) Women's 50 free (Tatarinova 24.87 EJR) + Women's 4×100 medley relay (4:02.72).
Critical structural difference: 6 of Russia's 11 golds in 2021 were relays (6 of the 8 relay events); only 5 were individual. In 2025 AIN had no relay medals at all.
Russia topped the European Junior Championships medal table every year from 2012 through 2021; in 2019 Kazan they won 36 medals.

Russia and Belarus were banned outright from the European Junior Championships from 2022 through 2024 following the invasion of Ukraine; 2025 Šamorín was their first return, as Neutral Individual Athletes.
MAJOR CURRENT CONTEXT: The 2026 European Junior Swimming Championships have already concluded — 7–12 July 2026, Olympiaschwimmhalle, Munich, Germany (52nd edition, 599 athletes).

On 5 February 2026 European Aquatics lifted all restrictions on Russian and Belarusian athletes in youth and junior categories, in both individual AND team events, allowing relay entries for the first time since 2021.
2026 Munich result: Neutral Athletes won 15 gold, 10 silver, 11 bronze = 36 medals, topping the medal table and taking the overall trophy (Italy 5-5-4 = 14; Great Britain 5-2-7 = 14).

2026 Neutral Athlete golds by day: Day 1 = 1, Day 2 = 3, Day 3 = 2, Day 4 = 1, Day 5 = 3, Day 6 = 5 (cumulative 1-4-6-7-10-15). Strongly back-loaded: 8 of 15 (53%) in the last two days, 5 of 15 (33%) on the final day.

2026 final-day (12 Jul) Neutral Athlete golds: Men's 100 back (Shcherbakov 53.99), Women's 100 breast (Anufrieva 1:08.10), Women's 400 free (Misharina 4:05.54 CR), Men's 400 free (Vekovishchev 3:44.58), Women's 4×100 medley relay (4:01.83 = CR).
